current_determination: A stochastic blocking kernel does not preserve reflection positivity merely by commuting with reflection and mapping positive-side observables to positive-side observables, because a Markov pullback is not multiplicative. A sufficient replacement is reflected Gram factorization; in particular, a reflection-covariant kernel that conditionally factorizes between positive and negative half-spaces preserves RP. A globally defined gauge-covariant soft link kernel of matrix-Fisher type, exp[beta*kappa*ReTr(V Q(U)^dagger)] with Haar normalization and local gauge-covariant matrix Q(U), evades the deterministic group-mean topology obstruction and has the correct weak-field Gaussian scaling. The remaining unproved interface is whether a reflection-adapted version of this soft gauge kernel closes inside Bałaban's 4d non-Abelian weak-field inductive estimates.
major_new_results: Reflection covariance plus positive-side locality is insufficient for a stochastic kernel; an explicit two-spin reflected kernel gives a negative RP form.
Reflected Gram factorization is a sufficient abstract condition for an RP fine measure to induce an RP coarse measure.
Conditional product factorization of a Markov kernel across reflection half-spaces is a practical sufficient criterion.
A soft gauge blocking kernel coupling coarse V directly to a gauge-covariant matrix Q[U] is globally defined and avoids logarithm/cut-locus/global-mean obstructions.
Because the blocking action is multiplied by beta~g^-2, a fixed-kappa soft kernel has weak-field width O(g) and becomes a hard saddle constraint as beta tends to infinity.

Rigorous non-gauge block-spin literature provides exact Gaussian-weight RG algebra, and an exact fermionic comparison shows exponential-weight blocking can have better uniform locality than delta blocking.
negative_results: Do not use K*Theta=Theta K* and K*(A_+) subset A_+ alone as a stochastic RP theorem.

The standard published fixed-point gauge blocking geometry is not installed as RP; its smeared Q receives contributions from an associated hypercube and the half-space support condition still has to be enforced/audited.
No source audited so far proves that replacing Bałaban's hard/nonlinear gauge average by the reflection-adapted soft matrix kernel preserves the full 4d non-Abelian inductive estimates.
